alternatives.root_cause: A cart-related feature flag was flipped in flagd, enabling a slow or failing code path in the cart service.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible in this topology and would leave an empty change log, but flag-driven cart faults usually surface as errors rather than pure latency, and nothing distinguishes it from a store slowdown without seeing the flag store and cart's error rate.

alternatives.root_cause: The cart service exhausted its connection pool or thread pool and queued incoming requests until callers timed out.
alternatives.why_not: Pool saturation is usually the consequence of a slow downstream rather than the first cause; without memory or thread metrics showing growth independent of the store, this is the symptom one layer up from the real fault.

verdict.summary: The cart service became slow because its backing store (valkey-cart, uninstrumented and therefore invisible in the graph) started responding slowly, and cart's request threads blocked waiting on it; the latency then propagated up through checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and the load-generator.
verdict.reasoning: All five alerts fire at the same timestamp, which means one slow thing saturated a synchronous call chain rather than five independent failures. The alerting set is exactly a call path: cart -> checkout -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> load-generator. Cart is the deepest member of that set and is the only one with no alerting dependency, so it is the origin rather than a victim. Its shared dependency flagd is almost certainly healthy: ad, recommendation and product-reviews also call flagd and none of them alert, and product-catalog, currency, payment, shipping and email are likewise quiet, so the fault is local to cart or to something only cart talks to. Cart's only private dependency is its key-value store, which is explicitly absent from the instrumented graph, so a store that went slow would show up exactly like this - cart reporting high latency itself (so its process is alive and emitting, ruling out freeze or partition) while everything downstream of it stays clean. Latency rather than error symptoms also argues against an outright crash, bad artifact or full disk.
open_questions: Cart's own latency breakdown: time spent in valkey/redis client spans versus time in its own handler
Valkey/redis server-side latency, memory pressure, eviction and connection counts during the window
Whether cart was returning errors or just slow responses, and whether its connection pool was saturated (queue wait time)
flagd evaluation latency and whether any cart-related flag changed value at 01:51
Cart container CPU throttling, heap/GC and thread pool metrics
Any deploy or config change to cart or its store in the preceding hour
